docs.text: asyncio uses cooperative multitasking — tasks must voluntarily yield control via await . A single long-running block of synchronous code will freeze everything. For CPU-heavy work inside async code, use asyncio.to_thread() (covered in Section 7).

docs.text: In Jupyter, we can await at the top level. In a normal .py script, you need asyncio.run() : # This is how you'd write it in a .py file: script_code = ''' import asyncio async def main(): print("Hello from async!") await asyncio.sleep(1) print("Done!") # This creates the event loop, runs main(), and cleans up asyncio.run(main()) ''' print ( "In a .py script, you use asyncio.run():" ) print ( script_code ) # In Jupyter, asyncio.run() won't work because a loop is already running. # Instead, just use 'await' directly: async def main (): print ( "Hello from async!" ) await asyncio . sleep ( 0.5 ) print ( "Done!" ) await main () In a .py script, you use asyncio.run(): import asyncio async def main(): print("Hello from async!") await asyncio.sleep(1) print("Done!") # This creates the event loop, runs main(), and cleans up asyncio.run(main()) Hello from async! Done!

docs.text: Write a coroutine countdown(name, seconds) that counts down from seconds to 0, printing each second. Then run two countdowns concurrently . async def countdown ( name , seconds ): """Count down from 'seconds' to 0, printing each second.""" # YOUR CODE HERE pass # Run two countdowns concurrently # YOUR CODE: use asyncio.gather to run countdown("A", 5) and countdown("B", 3) Solution async def countdown ( name , seconds ): for i in range ( seconds , 0 , - 1 ): print ( f " [ { name } ] { i } ..." ) await asyncio . sleep ( 1 ) print ( f " [ { name } ] DONE!" ) await asyncio . gather ( countdown ( "A" , 5 ), countdown ( "B" , 3 )) Notice how both countdowns print interleaved — they truly run concurrently!

docs.text: async def might_fail ( name , fail = False ): await asyncio . sleep ( 0.3 ) if fail : raise ValueError ( f " { name } failed!" ) return f " { name } ok" # Default: one failure crashes ALL tasks print ( "=== Default (crash on first error) ===" ) try : results = await asyncio . gather ( might_fail ( "A" ), might_fail ( "B" , fail = True ), might_fail ( "C" ), ) except ValueError as e : print ( f " Caught: { e } " ) print ( " All results lost!" ) # With return_exceptions=True: failures become return values print ( " \n === return_exceptions=True (resilient) ===" ) results = await asyncio . gather ( might_fail ( "A" ), might_fail ( "B" , fail = True ), might_fail ( "C" ), return_exceptions = True , ) for r in results : if isinstance ( r , Exception ): print ( f " FAILED: { r } " ) else : print ( f " OK: { r } " ) === Default (crash on first error) === Caught: B failed! All results lost! === return_exceptions=True (resilient) === OK: A ok FAILED: B failed! OK: C ok

docs.text: async def slow_upload ( filename ): print ( f " Uploading { filename } ..." ) await asyncio . sleep ( 2 ) print ( f " Upload complete: { filename } " ) return f " { filename } uploaded" async def main (): # create_task schedules the coroutine to run in the BACKGROUND task = asyncio . create_task ( slow_upload ( "photo.jpg" )) # We can do other work while it runs! print ( " Doing other work..." ) await asyncio . sleep ( 1 ) print ( " Still doing work..." ) # When we need the result, we await the task result = await task print ( f " Result: { result } " ) # We can also check state without awaiting task2 = asyncio . create_task ( slow_upload ( "video.mp4" )) await asyncio . sleep ( 0.5 ) print ( f " Is task2 done? { task2 . done () } " ) await task2 print ( f " Is task2 done? { task2 . done () } " ) await main () Doing other work... Uploading photo.jpg... Still doing work... Upload complete: photo.jpg Result: photo.jpg uploaded Uploading video.mp4... Is task2 done? False Upload complete: video.mp4 Is task2 done? True

docs.text: TaskGroup is the modern way to manage groups of tasks. It ensures all tasks complete or all are cancelled on error . import sys async def process_item ( item , delay ): await asyncio . sleep ( delay ) return f " { item } : processed" if sys . version_info >= ( 3 , 11 ): # TaskGroup is available in Python 3.11+ async with asyncio . TaskGroup () as tg : task1 = tg . create_task ( process_item ( "A" , 1 )) task2 = tg . create_task ( process_item ( "B" , 0.5 )) task3 = tg . create_task ( process_item ( "C" , 1.5 )) # All tasks guaranteed to be done here print ( f " { task1 . result () } " ) print ( f " { task2 . result () } " ) print ( f " { task3 . result () } " ) else : # Fallback for Python 3.10 and below print ( f " Python { sys . version_info . major } . { sys . version_info . minor } detected." ) print ( " TaskGroup requires Python 3.11+. Using gather instead:" ) results = await asyncio . gather ( process_item ( "A" , 1 ), process_item ( "B" , 0.5 ), process_item ( "C" , 1.5 ), ) for r in results : print ( f " { r } " ) Python 3.10 detected. TaskGroup requires Python 3.11+. Using gather instead: A: processed B: processed C: processed

docs.text: Write an async function that fetches data from multiple "servers" concurrently and returns only the successful results. Use gather with return_exceptions=True . async def query_server ( server_id ): """Simulates querying a server. Some servers will fail.""" delay = random . uniform ( 0.2 , 1.0 ) await asyncio . sleep ( delay ) if random . random () < 0.3 : # 30% failure rate raise ConnectionError ( f "Server { server_id } is down" ) return { "server" : server_id , "data" : f "response_ { server_id } " , "latency" : round ( delay , 2 )} async def fetch_all ( server_ids ): """ Query all servers concurrently. Return a tuple: (successes, failures) - successes: list of result dicts - failures: list of error strings """ # YOUR CODE HERE pass # Test it # successes, failures = await fetch_all(range(1, 11)) # print(f"Successes: {len(successes)}") # for s in successes: # print(f" Server {s['server']}: {s['data']} ({s['latency']}s)") # print(f"\nFailures: {len(failures)}") # for f in failures: # print(f" {f}") Solution async def fetch_all ( server_ids ): results = await asyncio . gather ( * [ query_server ( sid ) for sid in server_ids ], return_exceptions = True , ) successes = [ r for r in results if not isinstance ( r , Exception )] failures = [ str ( r ) for r in results if isinstance ( r , Exception )] return successes , failures successes , failures = await fetch_all ( range ( 1 , 11 )) print ( f "Successes: { len ( successes ) } " ) for s in successes : print ( f " Server { s [ 'server' ] } : { s [ 'data' ] } ( { s [ 'latency' ] } s)" ) print ( f " \n Failures: { len ( failures ) } " ) for f in failures : print ( f " { f } " )

CancelledError : # This is where you do cleanup! print ( " Job: CANCELLED! Cleaning up resources..." ) raise # Re-raise to properly cancel async def supervisor (): task = asyncio . create_task ( long_running_job ()) # Let it run for 1.5 seconds, then cancel await asyncio . sleep ( 1.5 ) print ( " Supervisor: Cancelling the job!" ) task . cancel () try : await task except asyncio . CancelledError : print ( " Supervisor: Job was successfully cancelled." ) await supervisor () Job: Starting... Job: Step 1/10 Job: Step 2/10 Job: Step 3/10 Supervisor: Cancelling the job! docs.text: Sometimes a task must not be cancelled (e.g., saving data to a database): async def critical_save ( data ): """This MUST complete even if the parent is cancelled.""" print ( f " Saving ' { data } ' to database..." ) await asyncio . sleep ( 1 ) print ( f " Save complete!" ) return True async def process_with_save (): print ( " Processing..." ) await asyncio . sleep ( 0.5 ) # Shield protects the inner coroutine from cancellation try : result = await asyncio . shield ( critical_save ( "important_data" )) print ( f " Save result: { result } " ) except asyncio . CancelledError : print ( " Process was cancelled, but save continues in background!" ) raise task = asyncio . create_task ( process_with_save ()) await asyncio . sleep ( 0.8 ) # Let it start the save task . cancel () try : await task except asyncio . CancelledError : pass # Give the shielded save time to complete await asyncio . sleep ( 1.5 ) print ( " All done." ) Processing... Saving 'important_data' to database... Process was cancelled, but save continues in background! Save complete! All done.

docs.text: wait gives you more control than gather : you can wait for the first task to complete, first to fail, or all . async def racer ( name , speed ): await asyncio . sleep ( speed ) return f " { name } finished in { speed } s!" tasks = [ asyncio . create_task ( racer ( "Alice" , 2.0 )), asyncio . create_task ( racer ( "Bob" , 1.0 )), asyncio . create_task ( racer ( "Charlie" , 1.5 )), ] # FIRST_COMPLETED: returns as soon as ONE task finishes done , pending = await asyncio . wait ( tasks , return_when = asyncio . FIRST_COMPLETED ) print ( "First to finish:" ) for task in done : print ( f " { task . result () } " ) print ( f " \n Still running: { len ( pending ) } tasks" ) # Clean up: wait for the rest remaining_done , _ = await asyncio . wait ( pending ) print ( " \n Remaining results:" ) for task in remaining_done : print ( f " { task . result () } " ) First to finish: Bob finished in 1.0s! Still running: 2 tasks Remaining results: Alice finished in 2.0s! Charlie finished in 1.5s!

docs.text: async def producer ( queue , n_items ): for i in range ( n_items ): item = f "item- { i } " await asyncio . sleep ( random . uniform ( 0.1 , 0.5 )) await queue . put ( item ) print ( f " [Producer] Put: { item } (queue size: { queue . qsize () } )" ) async def consumer ( queue , name ): while True : item = await queue . get () # Blocks until an item is available if item is None : # Poison pill = stop signal print ( f " [ { name } ] Received stop signal. Shutting down." ) break # Process the item process_time = random . uniform ( 0.2 , 0.8 ) print ( f " [ { name } ] Processing: { item } ..." ) await asyncio . sleep ( process_time ) print ( f " [ { name } ] Done: { item } ( { process_time : .1f } s)" ) queue . task_done () # Bounded queue: maxsize prevents producer from getting too far ahead queue = asyncio . Queue ( maxsize = 3 ) # Start 1 producer and 2 consumers prod = asyncio . create_task ( producer ( queue , 6 )) cons1 = asyncio . create_task ( consumer ( queue , "Worker-A" )) cons2 = asyncio . create_task ( consumer ( queue , "Worker-B" )) # Wait for producer to finish await prod # Wait for all items to be processed await queue . join () # Send stop signals await queue . put ( None ) await queue . put ( None ) await asyncio . gather ( cons1 , cons2 ) print ( " \n All work complete!" ) [Producer] Put: item-0 (queue size: 1) [Worker-A] Processing: item-0... [Worker-A] Done: item-0 (0.2s) [Producer] Put: item-1 (queue size: 1) [Worker-B] Processing: item-1... [Worker-B] Done: item-1 (0.4s) [Producer] Put: item-2 (queue size: 1) [Worker-A] Processing: item-2... [Producer] Put: item-3 (queue size: 1) [Worker-B] Processing: item-3... [Worker-A] Done: item-2 (0.7s) [Producer] Put: item-4 (queue size: 1) [Worker-A] Processing: item-4... [Producer] Put: item-5 (queue size: 1) [Worker-B] Done: item-3 (0.8s) [Worker-B] Processing: item-5... [Worker-A] Done: item-4 (0.4s) [Worker-B] Done: item-5 (0.5s) [Worker-A] Received stop signal. docs.text: # Shared counter WITHOUT a lock — race condition! counter_no_lock = 0 async def increment_unsafe ( n ): global counter_no_lock for _ in range ( n ): temp = counter_no_lock await asyncio . sleep ( 0 ) # Context switch point! counter_no_lock = temp + 1 counter_no_lock = 0 await asyncio . gather ( increment_unsafe ( 100 ), increment_unsafe ( 100 ), ) print ( f "Without lock: counter = { counter_no_lock } (expected 200)" ) # Shared counter WITH a lock — safe! counter_with_lock = 0 lock = asyncio . Lock () async def increment_safe ( n ): global counter_with_lock for _ in range ( n ): async with lock : # Only one coroutine can enter at a time temp = counter_with_lock await asyncio . sleep ( 0 ) counter_with_lock = temp + 1 counter_with_lock = 0 await asyncio . gather ( increment_safe ( 100 ), increment_safe ( 100 ), ) print ( f "With lock: counter = { counter_with_lock } (expected 200)" ) Without lock: counter = 100 (expected 200) With lock: counter = 200 (expected 200)

docs.text: A semaphore limits how many coroutines can access a resource simultaneously. Perfect for rate limiting API calls. async def call_api ( endpoint , semaphore ): async with semaphore : # Blocks if too many concurrent calls print ( f " Calling { endpoint } ..." ) await asyncio . sleep ( random . uniform ( 0.5 , 1.5 )) print ( f " Done: { endpoint } " ) return f " { endpoint } : ok" # Allow at most 3 concurrent API calls sem = asyncio . Semaphore ( 3 ) endpoints = [ f "/api/item/ { i } " for i in range ( 8 )] print ( "Processing 8 endpoints with max 3 concurrent: \n " ) start = time . time () results = await asyncio . gather ( * [ call_api ( ep , sem ) for ep in endpoints ]) print ( f " \n All done in { time . time () - start : .1f } s" ) print ( f "Results: { results } " ) Processing 8 endpoints with max 3 concurrent: Calling /api/item/0... Calling /api/item/1... Calling /api/item/2... Done: /api/item/1 Calling /api/item/3... Done: /api/item/2 Calling /api/item/4... Done: /api/item/3 Calling /api/item/5... Done: /api/item/0 Calling /api/item/6... Done: /api/item/6 Calling /api/item/7... Done: /api/item/4 Done: /api/item/5 Done: /api/item/7 All done in 2.8s Results: ['/api/item/0: ok', '/api/item/1: ok', '/api/item/2: ok', '/api/item/3: ok', '/api/item/4: ok', '/api/item/5: ok', '/api/item/6: ok', '/api/item/7: ok']

Takes 0.5 - 1.5 seconds.""" # YOUR CODE HERE: # 1. Acquire the semaphore # 2. Print that you're starting the download # 3. Sleep for a random time # 4. Return the file_id and download time pass # YOUR CODE: create a semaphore, download 20 files, print stats # Hint: Track total time, count successes, calculate average latency Solution async def download_file ( file_id , semaphore ): async with semaphore : delay = random . uniform ( 0.5 , 1.5 ) print ( f " Downloading file { file_id } ..." ) await asyncio . sleep ( delay ) return { "file" : file_id , "time" : round ( delay , 2 )} sem = asyncio . docs.text: Use async with when setup or teardown involves async operations. from contextlib import asynccontextmanager # Method 1: Class-based (implement __aenter__ and __aexit__) class AsyncTimer : """Times an async block.""" def __init__ ( self , label ): self . label = label async def __aenter__ ( self ): self . start = time . time () print ( f " [ { self . label } ] Timer started" ) return self async def __aexit__ ( self , exc_type , exc_val , exc_tb ): elapsed = time . time () - self . start print ( f " [ { self . label } ] Timer stopped: { elapsed : .2f } s" ) async with AsyncTimer ( "fetch" ) as timer : await asyncio . sleep ( 0.7 ) print ( " Doing work..." ) # Method 2: Decorator-based (simpler for most cases) @asynccontextmanager async def managed_connection ( db_name ): print ( f " Connecting to { db_name } ..." ) await asyncio . sleep ( 0.3 ) conn = { "db" : db_name , "status" : "connected" } try : yield conn # Hand the connection to the caller finally : print ( f " Disconnecting from { db_name } ..." ) await asyncio . sleep ( 0.1 ) print ( f " Disconnected." ) print () async with managed_connection ( "mydb" ) as conn : print ( f " Using connection: { conn } " ) [fetch] Timer started Doing work... [fetch] Timer stopped: 0.70s Connecting to mydb... Using connection: {'db': 'mydb', 'status': 'connected'} Disconnecting from mydb... Disconnected.

docs.text: import hashlib def cpu_heavy_work ( data ): """Simulates CPU-bound work (blocking!).""" result = data for _ in range ( 100_000 ): result = hashlib . sha256 ( result . encode ()) . hexdigest () return result [: 16 ] def blocking_io (): """Simulates blocking I/O (like a non-async database driver).""" time . sleep ( 1 ) return "data from blocking call" # BAD: calling blocking functions directly freezes the event loop # GOOD: run them in a thread with to_thread() print ( "Running blocking + async work concurrently:" ) start = time . time () results = await asyncio . gather ( asyncio . to_thread ( cpu_heavy_work , "hello" ), # Runs in a thread asyncio . to_thread ( blocking_io ), # Runs in a thread asyncio . sleep ( 1 ), # Runs in the event loop ) print ( f " \n Hash result: { results [ 0 ] } " ) print ( f "IO result: { results [ 1 ] } " ) print ( f "Total time: { time . time () - start : .1f } s (all ran concurrently!)" ) Running blocking + async work concurrently: Hash result: 3b2d9ab4b38fe0bc IO result: data from blocking call Total time: 1.0s (all ran concurrently!)

docs.text: Let's put everything together! We'll build a simulated web crawler that: 1. Starts from a list of seed URLs 2. Fetches pages concurrently (rate limited) 3. Extracts links from each page 4. Uses a queue to manage the crawl frontier 5. Respects a max depth and max pages limit import asyncio import random import time # Simulated web: maps URLs to their "content" and outgoing links FAKE_WEB = { "/" : [ "/about" , "/products" , "/blog" ], "/about" : [ "/about/team" , "/about/history" , "/" ], "/products" : [ "/products/1" , "/products/2" , "/products/3" ], "/blog" : [ "/blog/post-1" , "/blog/post-2" , "/" ], "/about/team" : [ "/about" ], "/about/history" : [ "/about" , "/" ], "/products/1" : [ "/products" , "/" ], "/products/2" : [ "/products" , "/products/1" ], "/products/3" : [ "/products" ], "/blog/post-1" : [ "/blog" , "/blog/post-2" ], "/blog/post-2" : [ "/blog" , "/" ], } async def fetch_page ( url , semaphore ): """Simulate fetching a web page.""" async with semaphore : delay = random . uniform ( 0.1 , 0.5 ) await asyncio . sleep ( delay ) if random . random () < 0.1 : # 10% chance of failure raise ConnectionError ( f "Failed to fetch { url } " ) links = FAKE_WEB . get ( url , []) size = random . randint ( 500 , 5000 ) return { "url" : url , "links" : links , "size" : size , "latency" : round ( delay , 3 )} async def crawl ( seeds , max_pages = 15 , max_concurrent = 3 ): """Crawl starting from seed URLs.""" visited = set () results = [] queue = asyncio . Queue () semaphore = asyncio . Semaphore ( max_concurrent ) # Seed the queue for url in seeds : await queue . put ( url ) async def worker ( worker_id ): while len ( visited ) < max_pages : try : url = queue . get_nowait () except asyncio . QueueEmpty : await asyncio . sleep ( 0.1 ) continue if url in visited : continue visited . add ( url ) try : page = await fetch_page ( url , semaphore ) results . append ( page ) print ( f " [W { worker_id } ] Crawled { url } " f "( { page [ 'size' ] } B, { page [ 'latency' ] } s, " f " { len ( page [ 'links' ]) } links)" ) # Add discovered links to the queue for link in page [ "links" ]: if link not in visited : await queue . put ( link ) except ConnectionError as e : print ( f " [W { worker_id } ] ERROR: { e } " ) # Run workers concurrently workers = [ asyncio . create_task ( worker ( i )) for i in range ( max_concurrent )] # Wait until enough pages crawled or workers finish while len ( visited ) < max_pages and not queue . empty (): await asyncio . sleep ( 0.1 ) # Give workers a moment to finish current pages await asyncio . sleep ( 1 ) # Cancel remaining workers for w in workers : w . cancel () return results # Run the crawler! print ( "Starting web crawler... \n " ) start = time . time () pages = await crawl ([ "/" ], max_pages = 11 , max_concurrent = 3 ) elapsed = time . time () - start total_bytes = sum ( p [ "size" ] for p in pages ) avg_latency = sum ( p [ "latency" ] for p in pages ) / len ( pages ) if pages else 0 print ( f " \n { '=' * 50 } " ) print ( f "CRAWL REPORT" ) print ( f " { '=' * 50 } " ) print ( f " Pages crawled: { len ( pages ) } " ) print ( f " Total data: { total_bytes : , } bytes" ) print ( f " Avg latency: { avg_latency : .3f } s" ) print ( f " Wall clock time: { elapsed : .1f } s" ) print ( f " Sequential est: ~ { sum ( p [ 'latency' ] for p in pages ) : .1f } s" ) Starting web crawler... [W0] ERROR: Failed to fetch / ================================================== CRAWL REPORT ================================================== Pages crawled: 0 Total data: 0 bytes Avg latency: 0.000s Wall clock time: 1.1s Sequential est: ~0.0s

docs.text: Build a complete async job scheduler that: Accepts jobs with priorities (higher priority runs first) Limits concurrency with a semaphore Supports timeouts per job Collects results and errors separately Reports statistics at the end import asyncio import random import time class AsyncJobScheduler : def __init__ ( self , max_concurrent = 3 , default_timeout = 5.0 ): self . max_concurrent = max_concurrent self . default_timeout = default_timeout self . jobs = [] # List of (priority, name, coro_func, timeout) self . results = [] self . errors = [] def add_job ( self , name , coro_func , priority = 0 , timeout = None ): """Add a job. Higher priority = runs first.""" # YOUR CODE HERE pass async def run_all ( self ): """Run all jobs respecting priority, concurrency, and timeouts.""" # YOUR CODE HERE: # 1. Sort jobs by priority (highest first) # 2. Create a semaphore # 3. For each job, create a task that: # a. Acquires the semaphore # b. Runs the coroutine with wait_for (timeout) # c. Stores result or error # 4. Gather all tasks # 5. Return (results, errors) pass # --- Test jobs --- async def fast_job (): await asyncio . sleep ( 0.3 ) return "fast result" async def slow_job (): await asyncio . sleep ( 3 ) return "slow result" async def flaky_job (): await asyncio . sleep ( 0.5 ) if random . random () < 0.5 : raise RuntimeError ( "Random failure!" ) return "flaky result" # --- Build and run --- scheduler = AsyncJobScheduler ( max_concurrent = 2 , default_timeout = 2.0 ) scheduler . add_job ( "Fast-1" , fast_job , priority = 1 ) scheduler . add_job ( "Fast-2" , fast_job , priority = 1 ) scheduler . add_job ( "Slow-1" , slow_job , priority = 0 ) # Will timeout! scheduler . add_job ( "Flaky-1" , flaky_job , priority = 2 ) # Highest priority scheduler . add_job ( "Flaky-2" , flaky_job , priority = 2 ) scheduler . add_job ( "Fast-3" , fast_job , priority = 1 ) # Run and print report # results, errors = await scheduler.run_all() # print(f"\nSuccesses: {len(results)}, Failures: {len(errors)}") Solution class AsyncJobScheduler : def __init__ ( self , max_concurrent = 3 , default_timeout = 5.0 ): self . max_concurrent = max_concurrent self . default_timeout = default_timeout self . jobs = [] self . results = [] self . errors = [] def add_job ( self , name , coro_func , priority = 0 , timeout = None ): timeout = timeout or self . default_timeout self . jobs . append (( priority , name , coro_func , timeout )) async def _run_job ( self , name , coro_func , timeout , semaphore ): async with semaphore : try : print ( f " [ { name } ] Starting..." ) result = await asyncio . wait_for ( coro_func (), timeout = timeout ) print ( f " [ { name } ] Success: { result } " ) self . results . append ({ "name" : name , "result" : result }) except asyncio . TimeoutError : print ( f " [ { name } ] TIMEOUT after { timeout } s" ) self . errors . append ({ "name" : name , "error" : "timeout" }) except Exception as e : print ( f " [ { name } ] FAILED: { e } " ) self . errors . append ({ "name" : name , "error" : str ( e )}) async def run_all ( self ): self . results . clear () self . errors . clear () # Sort by priority (highest first) self . jobs . sort ( key = lambda j : j [ 0 ], reverse = True ) sem = asyncio . Semaphore ( self . max_concurrent ) tasks = [ self . _run_job ( name , coro_func , timeout , sem ) for _ , name , coro_func , timeout in self . jobs ] start = time . time () await asyncio . gather ( * tasks ) elapsed = time . time () - start print ( f " \n { '=' * 40 } " ) print ( f "JOB REPORT ( { elapsed : .1f } s total)" ) print ( f " { '=' * 40 } " ) print ( f " Successes: { len ( self . results ) } " ) print ( f " Failures: { len ( self . errors ) } " ) for e in self . errors : print ( f " - { e [ 'name' ] } : { e [ 'error' ] } " ) return self . results , self . errors scheduler = AsyncJobScheduler ( max_concurrent = 2 , default_timeout = 2.0 ) scheduler . add_job ( "Fast-1" , fast_job , priority = 1 ) scheduler . add_job ( "Fast-2" , fast_job , priority = 1 ) scheduler . add_job ( "Slow-1" , slow_job , priority = 0 ) scheduler . add_job ( "Flaky-1" , flaky_job , priority = 2 ) scheduler . add_job ( "Flaky-2" , flaky_job , priority = 2 ) scheduler . add_job ( "Fast-3" , fast_job , priority = 1 ) results , errors = await scheduler . run_all ()

docs.text: async def f ( label , delay ): print ( f "start { label } " ) await asyncio . sleep ( delay ) print ( f "end { label } " ) await asyncio . gather ( f ( "X" , 1 ), f ( "Y" , 0.5 ), f ( "Z" , 0.1 )) Click to reveal! start X start Y start Z end Z (0.1s) end Y (0.5s) end X (1.0s) All start immediately (gather runs them concurrently). They end in order of their sleep duration.

docs.text: lock = asyncio . Lock () async def task_a (): async with lock : await task_b () async def task_b (): async with lock : print ( "done" ) await task_a () Click to reveal! **Yes, it deadlocks!** `task_a` holds the lock and calls `task_b`, which tries to acquire the same lock. Since `asyncio.Lock` is NOT re-entrant, `task_b` waits forever. Fix: restructure the code so the lock is not held across the call, or avoid nested lock acquisition.
docs.title: Q2: Will this code deadlock?

docs.text: async def fetch_all ( urls ): results = [] for url in urls : result = await fetch ( url ) results . append ( result ) return results Click to reveal! **It's sequential!** The `for` loop `await`s each `fetch()` one at a time. To fetch concurrently: async def fetch_all ( urls ): return await asyncio . gather ( * [ fetch ( url ) for url in urls ]) This is the most common asyncio performance mistake.

docs.text: Click to reveal! When you need to call a **blocking** function from async code without freezing the event loop. Common cases: - Non-async database drivers (sqlite3, psycopg2) - File I/O (open/read/write) - CPU-bound operations - Third-party libraries that don't support async # Instead of: data = open ( "big_file.csv" ) . read () # Blocks! # Do: data = await asyncio . to_thread ( open ( "big_file.csv" ) . read )
